Candidate gap: A. Integration. Capabilities exist across separate approaches
Evidence for: Tables 2.8–2.9: calibrated scoring (NEXUS), consequence pricing (H.-H. Chen), provenance (ProvenanceGuard; MCP policy-enforcement point), graduated verdicts (AgentTrust; LATTICE) are in different studies
Evidence against: NEXUS combines calibration and graduated responses (level A) and, per level-U evidence, costs, at the plan level
Decision: Retained only as a weak, record-bounded observation. A calibrated per-call probability combined with consequence-indexed losses at the action boundary was not reported in the examined records. Because the combination is specific and the review is record-level, its absence is not treated as evidence of originality

Candidate gap: B. Runtime action-boundary evaluation. Limited evidence combining multiple signals at the point of action
Evidence against: AgentTrust, the MCP policy-enforcement point, ToolSafe, DRIFT, SafeAgent and FinHarness combine several signals at or near the tool call
Decision: Not retained as stated. Its defensible residue, combination into a calibrated probability, is part of Gap A

Candidate gap: C. Behavioral/provenance contribution. Insufficient evidence separating the contribution of behavioral and provenance signals
Evidence for: Only three component-level tests found; they conflict (null session-tracker ablation vs. a 26.4-point cross-step-label effect); none inside a probabilistic estimator; none financial
Evidence against: The MCP policy-enforcement point does separate the contribution of cross-step labels in a rule-based enforcer (HIGH EVIDENCE)
Decision: Retained, narrowed. Limited and conflicting evidence on the contribution of behavioral and provenance evidence as inputs to a calibrated estimator for financial actions under indirect injection

Candidate gap: D. Financial-agent evidence. Limited verified evidence in executable financial settings
Evidence for: Four financial-context studies, all LIMITED EVIDENCE; the only quantitative runtime results cannot be confirmed against a maintained benchmark; general benchmarks with financial suites report no finance-specific analysis in the verified record
Evidence against: FinHarness shows the problem is recognized

Candidate gap: E. Evaluation decomposition. Insufficient evaluation separating security, benign utility, calibration or decision quality, intervention behavior and latency
Evidence for: Calibration reported for one deployed scorer (NEXUS); intervention rates by few studies; no study compares a consequence-aware decision with a consequence-independent baseline that shares its estimator
Evidence against: Several studies report more than attack success (MCP policy-enforcement point; LATTICE; NEXUS; ToolSafe)
Decision: Retained, narrowed. The missing element is the same-estimator comparison, with calibration reported separately from control and intervention rates reported
